title: Translate KV-autoscale postmortem actions into PRD requirements: ingress rate limits, fallback budgets, and cost telemetry
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Summary: This ticket captures product requirements to convert the KV-cache + autoscaling incident (INC-2026-031) postmortem actions into concrete PRD updates and acceptance criteria. The incident showed cascading autoscale and cache regen behavior that increased tail latency and monthly cost by ~32% for affected tenants. Postmortem recommendations include: (1) an ingress-level rate limiter and graceful backpressure policy, (2) a tenant-level fallback budget that can divert traffic to a lower-cost model variant when SLOs are at risk, (3) enhanced per-tenant cost telemetry and per-route cost tags, and (4) synthetic canaries and SLA gates for rollout. Scope: Update the serving PRD to include these features as required for all public runtime releases; define minimal viable UX for Console to expose fallback budgets and cost alerts; surface new observability metrics and alert thresholds. Out of scope: full billing UI redesign and third-party billing integrations (to be handled by Finance team). Deliverables: PRD text updates, acceptance criteria, a rollout checklist (canary + synthetic tests), and a telemetry tag spec for engineering to implement.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress rate limiter: documented API-level config with sensible defaults and a sandbox toggle; engineering has an integration test demonstrating rate limiting triggers on a synthetic traffic spike.

Fallback budgets: product schema for per-tenant fallback budgets (units: QPS and cost-per-minute) and console controls; regression test that routes >=95% of degraded requests to fallback model under controlled overload.
Cost telemetry: per-request cost tags added to existing traces; dashboards updated showing per-route and per-tenant cost deltas with daily and 7-day views.
Rollout gates: an automated canary that verifies latency and error-rate SLOs over 30 minutes; any breach triggers automated rollback and an on-call notification with playbook link.
Documentation: PRD section with runbook snippets, owner assignments, and links to postmortem and incident dashboards.
Performance budget: end-to-end median latency regression <= 5% and p99 regression <= 10% against baseline; cost increase for stable traffic <= 8% over baseline when feature enabled.
Operator acceptance: solutions engineering signs off on console UX for budget creation and alerting flow, and SRE signs off on observability coverage.
decisions: Implement ingress rate limiting in the router layer (instead of individual model servers) to ensure a single control point for backpressure and to reduce coordination complexity.
Fallback behavior will prefer model-variant downgrade first (e.g., quantized small model) and fall back to queued retries only if budget is exhausted, to optimize for latency and cost.
Expose fallback budget as both QPS and monetary budget in the Console; initial MVP will surface cost estimates rather than billable charges.
Synthetic canaries will run from multiple regions to catch cross-region cascading scenarios highlighted by the postmortem.
tradeoffs: Router-level rate limiting reduces complexity but adds an operational blast radius—mitigated by conservative defaults and a safe-mode bypass for emergency ops.
Fallback budgets prioritize latency and customer experience over absolute cost-savings; this increases short-term cost but prevents SLA violations and churn.
Adding per-request cost tags increases trace size and storage; tradeoff accepted because per-tenant cost visibility was a key postmortem finding requested by finance and customer success.
